claims.text: The as-deposited protective coating has an interpenetrating dual-phase FCC/BCC or FCC/B2 microstructure.
The FCC phase is soft and ductile, whereas the BCC or B2 phase is hard and high-strength.
The FCC/BCC or FCC/B2 interfaces in the coating are coherent.
Creep resistance is governed by a synergy between a dual-phase microstructure and dislocation pinning at coherent interfaces.
Coherent FCC/BCC phase boundaries act as dislocation-pinning sites.
The FCC phase generates dislocations during continuous elevated-temperature loading.
Coherent, high-strength BCC or B2 regions hinder dislocation motion in the FCC phase.
Dislocation pinning shifts strain accommodation across the FCC and BCC phases.
The proposed pinning and strain-partitioning mechanism lowers the coating's overall creep rate.
Reducing the BCC phase fraction or degrading interfacial coherence through modified processing provides a controlled comparison with the baseline coating.
A stress near 150 MPa is an appropriate sustained-stress test condition for the proposed coating.
A temperature range of 600–700°C is elevated and service-relevant for the proposed creep comparison.
Using an inert or protective atmosphere will minimize oxidation effects and isolate microstructural contributions to creep.
The baseline coating will have a slower creep rate than a coating with reduced BCC content or degraded interface coherence.
The baseline coating will enter tertiary creep later than the modified coating.
The proposed mechanism operates under moderate sustained stresses and elevated temperatures.
Excessive stress or temperature can destabilize or decohere the interfaces and diminish their creep-protective effect.
The critical BCC phase fraction and interface quality required for optimal creep resistance are not yet determined.
Grain size and phase instabilities during prolonged loading may also affect creep behavior.
Failure of the modified coating to show a statistically higher creep rate or earlier tertiary creep than the baseline would falsify the proposed role of coherent BCC boundaries.
